brief: A cabinet of three cells with two drawers, one of them shown pulled open.

requirements.requirement: A cabinet built from three cells (three bases in a row)
requirements.evidence: Three bases: piece (0,0) full, (0,1) half-n, (1,0) half-s. They form a triangle of cells, not a straight row; the two half bases carry the drawers. Joint bolts at (1,0) and (0,0) lock them. check_build: meshClash clear, no errors.
drawer:0#0,1#cut (stem s) on the cut face of half-n at (0,1), and drawer:0#1,0#cut (stem n) on the cut face of half-s at (1,0). get_build counts drawer: 2.

requirements.requirement: One of the two drawers shown pulled open
requirements.evidence: setDrawerOpen(open: true) was applied to drawer at (0,1) and returned ok, but get_build does not report open state, so the pulled-out position is not independently confirmed.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell cabinet: a full base at (0,0), with half bases at (0,1) and (1,0) that each take one drawer on their cut face. The drawers are "s" at (0,1) and "n" at (1,0). The drawer at (0,1) was set open. Joint bolts lock the cells. check_build is clean (meshClash clear, no errors). The three cells form a triangle, not a straight line. The open state of the drawer could not be read back from the build.

M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
